notes: The conceptual entries use whole record ports such as ctrl_i and frontend_o; the control-record rule therefore treats those ports as the boundary structural assets even when only one field carries the concept.
Bus request and response record fields are retained only as secondary paths or Not Reported entries because the rules bar them from being primary assets.
The prefetch buffer and decompressor are another-IP black boxes; their input-to-output value flows are judged using the stated black-box rule.

points.reason: The fetch PC is stored and updated here, is loaded from the control input, and its progress depends on response acknowledgement and fetch-state transitions.
The current fetch address is exposed directly on the instruction-bus request address assignment and can therefore be observed or altered at the boundary.
Fetched response data is directly placed on the prefetch-buffer write-data path, where it can be observed or changed before buffering.
The FIFO instance stores response words and returns them through rdata; its clear, write and read controls can alter or block instruction delivery.
The write-enable logic decides whether acknowledged response words enter the prefetch buffers, so it can corrupt or withhold the instruction stream.
Fetch-state and response-dependent control determines whether new instruction words are requested, accepted and advanced.
The disabled-generation path emits buffered instruction data and validity while its read control determines whether buffered words are consumed.
The enabled-generation path selects buffered instruction bits, sends them to the decompressor and controls buffer reads.
The another-IP decompressor receives the fetched compressed word and produces the instruction value used by the frontend; the black-box rule supplies the input-to-output flow.
The alignment state changes which buffered word and instruction form are selected and can therefore cause an incorrect or unavailable instruction.
This process selects compressed or decompressed instruction words and drives the valid, instruction and fault-related frontend outputs according to buffer availability and alignment.
The response error bit is copied into the buffered word, so changing ibus_rsp_i.err changes the eventual fault indication.
The FIFO stores the error bit together with each fetched word and returns it through its read-data output.
The non-RVC path directly returns the buffered error bit as frontend_o.fault.
The alignment selection chooses which buffered error bit is assigned to the fault output.
The fetch FSM stores the privilege mode from ctrl_i.cpu_priv and can therefore be influenced to associate a fetch with the wrong mode.
The stored privilege mode is copied directly into the instruction-bus request privilege field.
ctrl_i.cpu_debug is copied directly into the debug attribute of the outgoing fetch request, so changing the input changes the request semantics.
ctrl_i.if_fence is copied directly into the fence qualification of the outgoing fetch request, so changing it changes ordering behavior.
The halted status is selected from fetch.state and ipb.free, so corrupting either input can make the processor receive an incorrect stall indication.
